documents.title: Gallstones Question
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Quick question. A friend just had her gallbladder out and it made me think about my gallstones from years ago. I feel fine. Should I be avoiding fried food or anything? Do I need a scan?

documents.title: RE: Gallstones Question
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good question. Gallstones that aren't causing symptoms don't need a scan or surgery, and there's no special diet required. A lighter, lower-fat diet is good for weight anyway. What would change things: pain in the upper right or middle of the belly after eating that lasts more than half an hour, fever with belly pain, or yellowing of the skin or eyes. If any of that happens, call us the same day.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Weight check. She and a coworker did a step challenge Jan to April, averaging 7,000 steps. Down about a kilo since fall. Still eats out at lunch twice a week. Feels well, no new concerns.
Meds none. NKDA.
O: Vitals as charted. Comfortable. Heart RRR, lungs clear.
A/P: Obesity, BMI 32. Small loss, encouraged. Talked about adding two days of strength work. She asked about the weight-loss injections she sees advertised; went over how they work and the coverage hurdles; she prefers to keep going with lifestyle for now. Physical in October.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
32F, yearly physical.

Good year overall. Weight back up a little over the summer, roughly where she started with us. Busy at work, fine at home. No complaints on review: no chest pain, breathlessness, abdominal pain, bowel change, urinary symptoms, menstrual problems, skin changes, low mood.

Meds: none. NKDA.
SH: never smoker. Alcohol occasional, a drink or so a month. Administrative coordinator.
FH: unchanged (mother T2DM at 45).
PHQ-9: 1.

Exam: BP and other vitals as charted. Alert, well. Eyes, ears, throat normal. Neck without adenopathy or thyromegaly. Heart: regular, S1 S2 normal, no murmur. Lungs clear throughout. Abdomen soft, obese, nontender, no hepatomegaly. Extremities: no edema, pulses normal. Skin: no concerning lesions. Neuro grossly normal.

Assessment and plan:
1. Preventive care. Flu vaccine today. COVID updated dose at the pharmacy. Pap/HPV due 2026. Tdap through 2029.
2. Obesity (BMI about 32). Lifestyle; she declines medication. Revisit next year.
3. Labs: CBC, CMP, lipids, A1c (family history), TSH.

See in one year.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Wanda - everything from Wednesday came back normal. Blood count, kidney, liver, thyroid and cholesterol are all fine and your A1c is still in the normal range. Have a good fall.

documents.title: Pharmacy Immunization Notification
documents.author: pharmacy
documents.body: Vaccine administered: COVID-19 mRNA (Moderna), 2024-2025 formula, 0.5 mL intramuscular, right deltoid, 11/05/2024. No adverse event reported at the pharmacy.

documents.title: Insurance Update
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Patient called with new insurance cards for 2025 (same carrier, PPO plan, new member ID through employer). Front and back scanned from her upload. Eligibility verified. Membership renewal for the year processed.

documents.title: Positive Pregnancy Test
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Good morning! I took a home pregnancy test this weekend and it was positive, and another one this morning was too. My last period started March 1st. I stopped drinking as soon as I saw the first one. What should I do next? Do I see you first or go straight to an OB?

documents.title: RE: Positive Pregnancy Test
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Congratulations! Let's see you next week to confirm, start a prenatal vitamin and go over the early basics, and I'll send the referral to an obstetrics practice the same day. Until then: no alcohol (you've done that), no smoking exposure, limit caffeine to a cup or two of coffee, and acetaminophen is the safe choice if you need something for a headache. Call us for bleeding or severe pain. The front desk will reach out to book.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - Pregnancy Confirmation
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here after two positive home tests. LMP 3/1/25, regular cycles, which puts her at 6 weeks 4 days, EDD 12/6/25. Mild nausea in the mornings, eating fine. No bleeding, cramping or pain. Stopped alcohol when she tested. Never smoker. No meds.

OB history: G2P1001 now; first pregnancy uncomplicated, term vaginal birth.

Urine hCG in office: positive.

Exam: vitals as charted; BP normal. Well appearing. Abdomen soft, nontender.

A/P:
1. Intrauterine pregnancy presumed, about 6.5 weeks by dates. Prenatal vitamin with iron daily starting today. Reviewed food safety, no alcohol, acetaminophen rather than NSAIDs, and to call or go to L&D triage for heavy bleeding or one-sided pain.
2. Obesity, pre-pregnancy BMI 32, and mother with type 2 diabetes: both are reasons for the OB to consider earlier glucose testing; noted in the referral.
3. Referral to obstetrics placed today; first OB visit expected around 8 to 10 weeks.
She can message any time in the meantime.

documents.title: Referral Sent - Obstetrics
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: OB referral with yesterday's visit note faxed to the obstetrics group. They called back and booked her new OB intake for 4/30 with a dating ultrasound. Patient informed by phone, she has the address.

documents.title: Update - It's Twins
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi! Just wanted to let you know, the ultrasounds at the OB show it's TWINS. My grandmother had twins so I guess it runs in the family. They say I'm going to get extra ultrasounds with the high-risk doctors. I'm a little overwhelmed but excited. Still taking the prenatal every day.

documents.title: RE: Update - It's Twins
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: What news! Thank you for telling me. The OB team and the high-risk (maternal-fetal medicine) doctors will lead your pregnancy care, and I'll get their notes. I'm still here for anything outside the pregnancy, or if you just want to talk something through. Keep up the vitamin.

conditions.label: Monochorionic monoamniotic twin pregnancy, second trimester
Gestational diabetes mellitus in pregnancy, diet controlled
Complete placenta previa without hemorrhage, second trimester

documents.title: Maternal-Fetal Medicine Visit Letter
documents.author: maternal-fetal medicine
documents.body:
Maternal-Fetal Medicine - Visit Summary to Primary Care
Date of visit: 08/28/2025
Re: Wanda Figueroa, DOB 07/06/1992

Dear colleague,

We saw your patient today for scheduled prenatal care. She is a 33-year-old G2P1001 at 25 weeks 5 days (LMP 03/01/2025, concordant with first-trimester ultrasound; EDD 12/06/2025) carrying monochorionic monoamniotic twins, followed with serial ultrasound in our unit since the first trimester.

Until this month the pregnancy had gone smoothly. On early glucose testing, done because of her pre-pregnancy BMI of 32, her mother's type 2 diabetes and the twin gestation, she was diagnosed with gestational diabetes on 08/13/2025; she has met with our dietitian and is managing with diet for now.

Today she reports frequent movement from both babies. She denies any vaginal bleeding, fluid leakage or contractions. She continues to work full time at a desk job.

Medications: prenatal vitamin with iron daily.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Family history: mother with type 2 diabetes (onset 45); maternal grandmother with a twin pregnancy.
Social: never smoker; no alcohol since the pregnancy was confirmed.

Exam: BP 120/75, HR 88. General exam unremarkable. Fundal height 32 cm, roughly what a singleton would measure at 32 weeks and in keeping with a twin gestation. Fetal heart tones 140 and 142 bpm.

Ultrasound today: monochorionic monoamniotic twin gestation, both fetuses with cardiac activity and concordant growth. The placenta covers the internal cervical os completely.

Assessment:
1. Monochorionic monoamniotic twin pregnancy at 25w5d.
2. Complete placenta previa, no bleeding to date.
3. Gestational diabetes, diet controlled.
4. Obesity, pre-pregnancy BMI 32.

Plan and counseling: We spent a long time today with her on what a single shared sac means for twins: the higher risk of cord problems between the babies, of preterm birth and of losing one or both pregnancies, and why we watch these pregnancies so closely. Her questions were answered. With the previa she is on pelvic rest and knows to come in at once for any bleeding. She will log fasting and post-meal glucose and return in 2 weeks for diabetes review. Ongoing frequent ultrasound surveillance here.

Thank you for allowing us to share her care.

Maternal-Fetal Medicine
